#!/usr/bin/env sh
# PLN-1772 Phase 2 - typecheck what this branch actually changed.
#
# The commit hooks used to run the FULL graph on every commit: 31s warm, and
# ~3 minutes across a 6-commit PR proving the same thing over and over. That is
# what makes `--no-verify` attractive, and a bypassed hook takes the source-gate
# ratchets with it. The affected graph costs ~1s when a change does not reach a
# typed package.
#
# The affected filter cannot see a dependent outside the graph it computed, so
# this is a commit-tier signal, never the gate. ISS-8050: what it is NOT is a
# tier with a full-graph safety net under it locally. `.husky/pre-push` now runs
# `pnpm verify --scope=push`, which drops the full-graph typecheck because CI
# runs the identical command on the merge ref. `pnpm verify` with no scope is
# the only local command that still compiles the whole graph.
#
# The filter comes from scripts/affected-filter.sh, shared with
# `test:affected`: the branch's changes since its merge-base with origin/main,
# plus their dependents (ISS-11856). Without that merge-base turbo cannot
# compute an affected set at all, so fall back to the full serial run rather
# than silently typechecking nothing.
set -u

concurrency=${TURBO_TYPECHECK_CONCURRENCY:-1}

# Absolute, not cwd-relative: the sibling hooks cd to the repo root before
# calling in, but nothing guarantees every caller does, and a probe that
# silently fails to resolve turns the empty-graph guard off while the run it
# guards still proceeds.
repo_root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || printf '.')
TURBO_BIN="$repo_root/node_modules/.bin/turbo"
# The probe module and the loader that runs it ship WITH this script, so both
# resolve beside it. turbo above resolves from the repo root instead, because
# which workspace to size is a property of the checkout, not of this file.
script_dir=$(dirname "$0")
PROBE_MODULE="$script_dir/lint/affected-typecheck-tasks.ts"
TSX_BIN="$script_dir/../node_modules/.bin/tsx"

# Typecheck tasks turbo would really execute. Probed through turbo's own binary
# rather than `pnpm turbo`: pnpm's startup dominates this tier, and paying it
# twice per commit is what makes a hook worth bypassing.
affected_task_count() {
    { [ -x "$TURBO_BIN" ] && [ -x "$TSX_BIN" ]; } || return 1
    "$TURBO_BIN" typecheck --filter="$AFFECTED_FILTER" --dry=json 2>/dev/null |
        "$TSX_BIN" "$PROBE_MODULE"
}

if ! AFFECTED_FILTER=$(sh "$script_dir/affected-filter.sh"); then
    printf '\033[2mtypecheck: %s; running the full graph.\033[0m\n' "$AFFECTED_FILTER"
    exec pnpm turbo typecheck --concurrency="$concurrency"
fi

task_count=$(affected_task_count) || task_count=''

# An empty affected graph exits 0 having compiled nothing, and turbo's own
# summary ("Tasks: 0 successful, 0 total") reads like a pass. Say that out loud
# rather than printing success; refusing the commit would only earn a bypass.
# Saying it is now the WHOLE local signal, not a warning ahead of one: pre-push
# no longer runs the full graph either (ISS-8050).
if [ "$task_count" = "0" ]; then
    printf '\033[1;33m== typecheck: NOTHING WAS TYPECHECKED ==\033[0m\n'
    printf 'No affected package has a typecheck task, so tsc never ran. This is NOT a pass.\n'
    printf 'No local tier runs the full graph by default: pre-push runs `pnpm verify --scope=push`, which drops it. Run `pnpm verify` with no scope to compile it here; otherwise CI is the first thing that will. `scripts/**` is in neither tier - typecheck it against its own project, e.g. `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p scripts/<area>/tsconfig.json`.\n'
    exit 0
fi

# Never silent: a probe that stops answering would otherwise retire the guard
# above for every commit in the repo with no diagnostic at all.
if [ -z "$task_count" ]; then
    printf '\033[2mtypecheck: could not size the affected graph; running it rather than assuming it is empty.\033[0m\n'
fi

exec pnpm turbo typecheck --filter="$AFFECTED_FILTER" --concurrency="$concurrency"
